about: Confirmation sitting for the DreamSim yardstick (docs/yardstick-perceptual-prereg-2026-11-08.md): every one of the pro_baseline.JOBS logos drawn at the pro's own garment and width, six one-flag arms chosen for a VISIBLE difference in a monochrome render, so Kent decides a side and the instrument gets decided pairs. Pre-registered; nothing here was rendered or scored when it was committed. NOT blind to prior judging: see rejudge_pro_jobs.
base_note: Today's main defaults, no overrides. Every arm turns ONE flag away from its default.

drop_order_note: Documentation, read by a person: prepare does NOT consume this key. Over budget (more than 70 live pairs), remove the logos in this order, one at a time, by editing spec.json as a dated amendment written before any pick exists, then rebuild. Whole logos only; every artwork cluster keeps its lead job until last.

apex_cut_on.variable: construction at an acute tip (M's V, W apexes, a pointed A or N): ON sews the tip as ONE piece of crosses along the line of text; OFF mitres two fanning columns (flag OFF today)
apex_cut_on.basis: Memory apex-cut-2026-10-25 (and apex-walk-2026-10-27): the pro sews every such tip as one piece, crosses within 16 deg of the line of text; built OFF on numbers against the pro, judged in the preview, never flipped.

script_drawn_width_on.variable: script where strokes crowd: a cross side that would run over 1.0 mm into another stroke stops at the art's drawn half-width; OFF reaches the traced polygon (flag OFF today)
script_drawn_width_on.basis: Memory script-strokes-2026-10-26: Bridge hat lays 24.9 percent of the word's thread twice against the pro's 10.5; ON 19.3. Only crowded script words can differ.

white_fields_fill_on.variable: a sewn white field: ON sews it as a fill at the pro's 22 deg under the outline; OFF leaves it to the Column lane as lettering (flag OFF today)
white_fields_fill_on.basis: Memory white-faces-fill-2026-10-25: the pro sews those faces as a 22 deg tatami under the outline; ours sewed them as Column-lane letters (Becker 8.4x slower). Only art with a sewn white field can differ.

border_by_size_off.variable: a plain fill 6 mm and up: ON sews a satin border at the pro's median width round it; OFF leaves the bare fill (flag ON today)
border_by_size_off.basis: Memory border-by-size-2026-10-23 and border-by-size-colour-seams-2026-10-28: ON by Kent 2026-10-23 on the pro-count numbers; plain fills at 6 mm and up are a coin flip per design in the pro's files.

fine_bars_satin_off.variable: a thin free-standing ink bar: ON sews one satin bar at its drawn width plus pull; OFF sews a hollow bean ring (flag ON today)
fine_bars_satin_off.basis: Memory fine-bars-satin-2026-10-25: the pro satins every such bar (5 of 5 artworks), 37 of 38 target regions cure; ON by Kent 2026-10-26 on the wave-3 flip sheet.

bean_only_lines_off.variable: what gets a bean: ON keeps a bean only for LINES the art draws (smallest dimension 1.2 mm or less), letters and solids take the ordinary ladder; OFF beans by size as before (flag ON today)
bean_only_lines_off.basis: Memory bean-census-2026-10-27: the reference beans 8 of 1,101 regions, ours 137 (111 small letters); ON by Kent 2026-10-27 (#1161), region kappa -0.014 to 0.129.

reserve_arms.variable: an untagged lettering-thin shape inside a sewn white field: ON rides it over the host thread so the white does not sew over it; OFF as today (flag OFF today)
reserve_arms.basis: Memory mfab-and-recheck-2026-11-06 and underfill-knockouts-2026-10-26; built OFF 2026-11-05 (Kent: keep OFF, fix the superpixel merge). Reads only where riders are, so MFab-type art.
reserve_arms.name: untagged_riders_on

reserve_arms.variable: a dark-read stroke on a pale ground: ON sews it as a bean along its skeleton after its ground; OFF is the engine before the flip (flag ON today)
reserve_arms.basis: Memory dark-ink-bean-2026-10-28: ON 2026-10-29 by Kent (Pooh). Few pro jobs carry a dark read, so likely inert; a reserve only.
reserve_arms.name: dark_ink_bean_off

manipulation.rule: An arm passes when it changes the stitch stream on at least `min_live_logos` logos and, on at least half of the logos it changes, every `moves` metric moves the stated way by its threshold and every `holds` metric moves by less. No arm here registers a `moves` or `holds` metric, so the check is only that it changes the stitch stream on enough logos; whatever moves is a measurement. A byte-identical logo is not a pair. A failing arm is replaced ONCE by the first unused reserve of its stratum (`settle_arms`), before any picture is seen; a reserve that fails too stays, flagged passes=false, and the analysis reads the leads on all live pairs and on the passing arms alone.

primary.why: #847's one lead independent of trims (+0.16 ties in, one sitting's)
#847's reversed hypothesis, direction written down in advance: he picks FEWER long stitches
his notes say denser is better; #847 found no support
the control: the one instrument that cleared chance in #842 and #847; if it does not replicate here nothing else in this sitting is read

analysis.ci: percentile bootstrap, 10000 resamples, seed 20261108, over pairs AND over designs (the `design` key of each logo)
analysis.reading_rule: the registered reading is the DreamSim claim rule in PRE-REGISTRATION.md; the analyse step's leads are secondary and cannot carry a claim
analysis.population: live pairs (arm differs from base). Identical and repeat pairs are controls and enter no agreement statistic.

pro_distance.population: A: the live pairs on the pro_baseline.JOBS logos
pro_distance.reading: distance = |ours - pro| (pro_pooled.distance), lower is closer, beside the same figures as a plain cost; kappa, both intervals (pairs and designs), n; pairs scoring his pick farther from the pro are counted
pro_distance.readers: pro_pair.pro_counts and pro_baseline.needle_up on ours.dst (designs/<logo>__<arm>.dst) and on the pro's DST, the same code on both
